Marissa / team —

Quick technical notes to include in the response doc (I copied the Measurement_Methodology.md into the draft):

1) Uptime measurement
- Definition: Monthly Uptime % = (Total Minutes in Month - Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month. Downtime is any period when the Redwood API is unable to accept or serve requests for a customer because the customer-specific control-plane routing or inference runtime returns 5xx or connection failures.
- Measurement points: we measure at the customer-specific API ingress (regional endpoints that route to the customer's pinned capacity or hosted pool). We also run synthetic health probes from three regions (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1) to detect regional network issues.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance (we provide >=48 hours notice for planned maintenance windows), customer-side networking outages, scheduled scaling events >30m (where capacity reconverges), and force majeure.

2) Latency SLOs and profile definitions
- Interactive (short): <=512 tokens total request+response. Typical targets: p50 <= 150ms (dedicated), p95 <= 320ms (dedicated). Hosted API expected p95 <= 450ms depending on model & load.
- Conversational / medium: 512-2048 tokens. Expect p95 to vary by model and cache-hit rates; we include guidance per-model in the model catalog.
- Batch/async: for large token counts we provide throughput SLO guidance (tokens/sec) instead of single-request latency.
- Measurement: latency measured at inference service (time from request accepted by runtime to last token produced) and reported as p50/p95/p99 over a rolling 30-day window. We can provide per-route and per-model breakdowns on request.

3) Service credits calculation (ops note)
- Credits will be calculated as a percentage of monthly recurring charges for the affected service for the month in question. We cap cumulative credits to 100% of monthly fee.

4) Data residency / per-customer measurement
- We can pin measurement to region-specific ingress and provide per-tenant telemetry for Acme Health if they opt into dedicated capacity or Private deployment.

I'll attach the Measurement_Methodology.md draft. If Acme needs stricter latency bounds we should confirm model choices and whether they want Dedicated capacity.

- Dev

Attachments: Measurement_Methodology.md (md)

Team —

Draft service credit schedule and legal points to include in the RFP response:

1) Service Credit Tiers (monthly uptime percentage measured per account):
- >= 99.95%: No credit
- < 99.95% and >= 99.00%: 10% credit of monthly recurring charges for the impacted service
- < 99.00% and >= 95.00%: 25% credit
- < 95.00%: 50% credit

2) Calculation and claim process
- Customer must submit a claim within 30 days of the end of the month in which the alleged SLA failure occurred, including supporting logs (we will provide per-tenant measurement output).
- Credits are applied to the customer's next invoice; credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures.
- Cap: cumulative credits in a 12-month period capped at 100% of annual fees associated with the affected service.

3) Exclusions (to mirror technical): scheduled maintenance (>=48 hrs notice), customer network outages, and third-party incidents (cloud provider outages, backbone issues) that are demonstrably outside Redwood's control.

4) Reporting and RCA
- For any outage resulting in credits >=25% we will provide a written root cause analysis within 10 business days.

5) Negotiable items
- We can accept adjustments for enterprise customers (longer notice windows for maintenance, stricter calculation granularity) if contractually agreed and tied to Dedicated or Private deployment commitments.

I'll add these items to the Redwood_SLA_2026_v1.pdf and return a redline if Acme sends a procurement template.

—Evelyn
